03/13.04.2023

The present writ petition has been filed for issuance of direction up
concerned respondents to pay appropriate compensation to the petitioners for acquisition of their
lands appertaining to Khata No. 36, Plot Nos. 2268 & 2269, Mouza-Jareya, Thana No. 319,
P.S-Namkum, District-Ranchi, measuring an area of about 0.322 Hectare (82.046 Decimals) which
were acquired by the respondents for construction of Nh-33.
Learned counsel for the petitioners submits that the aforesaid lands are the ancestral property of the petitioners.

A copy of the genealogical table annexed as Annexure-2 to the writ petition would suggest that the petitioner Nos. 1 & 2 are the nephews of the recoded tenant-Late Gansa Munda whereas the petitioner No.3 is his grandson.

In the process of acquisition of the said lands vide Land Acquisition Case No. 29/14-15, Award Nos. 47 & 48 were prepared in the names of Late Gansa Munda and others and pursuant thereto, the notices dated 24.02.2016 were issued.
Despite the said fact, no compensation has yet been paid to the petitioners/lawful claimants.
The petitioners represented various authorities in this regard, however, the same were not responded which has compelled them to prefer the present writ petition.

sentences.text: A counter affidavit has been filed on behalf of the respondent No.2 stating inter alia that a cumulative amount of Rs.27.70 Crore has been deposited with the respondent No.4 for acquisition of the said lands, as would be evident from letter No. 1154 dated 02.11.2016 issued to the respondent No.4 and hence the said respondent being the competent authority under the National Highways Act, 1956 has to look into the petitioners' aforesaid grievance.

Having heard learned counsel for the parties and keeping in view the nature of the prayer made in the present writ petition, without entering into the merit of the case, the petitioners are given liberty to prefer a fresh representation on the present issue before the respondent No.4.

On receipt of the said representation, the respondent No.4, after verifying the relevant records and on providing an opportunity of hearing to the petitioners and other concerned person(s), if so required, shall take an appropriate informed decision in accordance with law within four weeks from the date of filing of the said representation.
The present writ petition is accordingly disposed of with the aforesaid liberty and direction.

Satish/- (RAJESH SHANKAR, J)
